findings.title: Coverage threshold uses an exempted subset instead of all 24 surfaces
findings.detail: The task requires per-primitive adoption to be the number of actual consumer surfaces divided by 24, with every named primitive at or above 90%. The implementation filters each primitive through surface.eligible and divides adopted by that smaller set. The passing output exposes the false-positive behavior: mg-tabs=11/11 (100.0%), mg-metric-grid=14/14 (100.0%), mg-hero=22/22 (100.0%), and state=23/23 (100.0%); against the required denominator of 24, tabs and metric-grid are far below 90%. The manifest exemptions therefore defeat the fail-closed acceptance rule.

findings.title: Route-root attribution can be assembled from unrelated main elements
findings.detail: The visitor accumulates ownershipValues and accentValues across every <main> in the file, then checks those sets independently and accepts data-page-prelude anywhere in the AST. A file with ownership on one nested or unrelated <main>, accent on another, and prelude elsewhere passes even though its route root does not carry both required attributes. The guard must identify the route-root JSX element and validate ownership plus accent on that same element.

findings.title: Frozen lane changes files forbidden by the task's exclusive write scope
findings.detail: The task grants exclusive source write scope only to scripts/qa/checkMediaPrimitiveAdoption.ts, but the frozen diff also changes package.json and includes checkMediaPrimitiveCoverage.ts and checkMediaPrimitiveEnhancements.ts in the reviewed lane. package.json additionally wires route-matrix and shell-contract commands unrelated to this task. This is an explicit scope violation.
